causebase_summary: Accelerated Evolution - The Break Inc. is a volunteer-run not-for-profit based in Caulfield, Melbourne, Victoria, that provides mental health and wellbeing recovery programs. data.SummaryOfActivities: Biopixel Oceans Foundation continued conducting shark research around general movements and the impact of human and shark interaction for shark conservation and public safety. The program has been running since 2018 in the Whitsundays and 2021 at Northwest Island Capricorn Bunker group. Knowledge has been used to inform water users of shark behaviour (e.g. complementing Fisheries Queensland Shark Smart program) so they can make informed choices of when/how they undertake marine activities. BOF consolidated the previous 4 years of filed work on whale shark aggregation on the east coast of Australia. Producing a report for the QLD government threatened species department, and 4 scientific papers (resulting in 7 papers to date). Aa an extension, we discovered the first manta ray parturition site in Australia, located off Weipa in the Gulf of Carpentaria. Population studies of bull and tiger sharks on Australia s east coast continued. Under our lifeboat species banner, research assessing the health of species threatened internationally and believed to be healthy populations in Australia was conducted. This includes collecting data on population status and essential habitats for 20 species of shark and rays. Through the large-scale animal movement program BOF have electronically tagged >1300 animals and manage the largest QLD array ever deployed in QLD. BOF has worked with ReShark (ReWild) on the STAR project, collecting data and semen samples in Australia for breeding and restocking of leopard sharks in Indonesia https://www.reshark.org/star-project. We also facilitated the first expedition for ReShark to find and study Shark Rays, a highly threatened species that is the next candidate for the Rewilding program. BOF is also partnering with Queensland Fisheries, the University of Central Queensland, University of Sunshine Coast and game fishing clubs providing research to manage key commercial fishery species, such as black jewfish Protonibea diacanthaus and mud crabs and recreational fished species e.g. sailfish and dolphinfish. Three publications were produced in 2025. These activities helped BOF achieve its aim of supporting the protection and enhancement of our oceans through fostering a better understanding of shark behaviour and providing a data driven basis for determining shark policy. The continued whale shark and Omuras whale shark work continue to provide key findings for management in Australia and internationally. The Foundation shares live movement information of sharks to our public available biotracker https://biotracker.tv/. Biopixel work with Traditional owner groups, training them in scientific methods for understanding food web ecology and tracking totem species. In the last 2 years, seven post graduate students BOF staff have supervised or helped supervise have graduated. These public outputs support the Foundation's aim to foster education and a better understanding of the need for environmental protection and preservation.

data.SummaryOfActivities: Seniors Rights Service is a not-for-profit community organisation that has been supporting the rights of older people for 40 years. Our mission is to empower older people to assert their rights through accessible, free and confidential legal services, aged care advocacy and information services across New South Wales. Our role is to advocate for older people, assisting them to claim their rights and support them in exercising those rights so that they enjoy a rich life as seniors and respected members of the community with dignified and equitable access to the care and support they need. In all our endeavours, Seniors Rights Service adheres to principles that empower older people as rights holders, provide high quality and timely services, ensure equitable access for seniors, collaborate with other organisations and work with civil society to foster respect for older individuals and their rights. Seniors Rights Service is an accredited specialist community legal centre that provides assistance to older people in NSW. Our legal service provides free legal advice, casework assistance, information, referral and community legal education. We can advise on matters relating to human rights, planning for the future, consumer rights, retirement living, strata living and boarding house legal advice. Additionally, our aged care advocacy addresses the needs of older people receiving Commonwealth funded aged care services at home and in residential care. We provide targeted rights based information to a diverse range of older people and through information sessions, forums and tailored advice, we continue to serve the diverse needs of our community, striving for a society where older individuals are respected, valued and empowered. We prioritise engagement with older people who are:   disadvantaged and vulnerable   First Nations people   from culturally and linguistically diverse backgrounds   from the LGBTQ+ community   living in regional, rural and remote locations
